title: Mirabel and the Terminal
premise: Wendell Brightwater, sole caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent thirty years running supply routes between colonies that severed contact after the Fleet Consolidation. When a distress signal arrives in a language officially extinct for two centuries, he traces it to Vessel Meridian, a ghost ship whose crew claims their colony was massacred by the Fleet itself — and then erased from every record. Bound by an old caretaker's oath to preserve life in all its forms, Wendell becomes an unlikely archivist of a crime no one will admit happened. As the fleet's fragile truce expires, he must smuggle the ship's surviving testimony — and its last living witness, a woman who remembers everything the archives forgot — to a neutral assembly before the evidence, and they, are destroyed. He succeeds at terrible cost: the truth is entered into the record, but Wendell surrenders his ship and his solitary freedom to stand as living proof.
about_author: Zephyrine Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing declassified shipping logs before turning to fiction. They write from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where they insist the fog improves sentence structure.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Establishes his solitary life tending Earth's seed vault and his annual circuit between silent colonies. The emotional beat is loneliness worn as routine — until a signal arrives in a language that should not exist, and his careful order cracks open.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Wendell deciphers enough of the distress signal to realize it predates the Consolidation purge. His POV; wonder curdling into dread as he recognizes the transmission's origin coordinates match a colony listed as never having existed.

chapters.title: Vessel Meridian
chapters.summary: Wendell docks with the derelict-turned-alive ship. Alternating POV with Sefa Ilori, the last witness, who tests him before trusting him. Emotional beat: two isolated people recognizing each other's exile.

chapters.title: What the Crew Remembered
chapters.summary: Sefa recounts the massacre at Calloway Reach through recorded testimony. Wendell cross-checks against fleet charts and finds the colony scrubbed clean. Beat: horror at how thoroughly a people can be unwritten.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Oath
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV flashback to his swearing-in at the vault: to preserve, not to judge. He realizes preserving memory means becoming evidence himself. Beat: duty redefined against the institution that gave it to him.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet POV via intercepted communiqués — Commander Ashen Vale learns a caretaker ship has gone off-route. Beat: cold institutional menace; the countdown to truce expiry begins, ninety days.

chapters.title: Cargo of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sefa and Wendell load the ship's testimony archive aboard his hauler, disguised as seed stock. Quiet chapter of intimacy and trust. Beat: love beginning where shared purpose takes root.

chapters.title: The Port That Pretends
chapters.summary: They stop at Halcyon Drift for supplies; a portmaster who owes Wendell warns them fleet auditors are asking questions. Beat: paranoia, first betrayal's shadow, and a small kindness that keeps them moving.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Records
chapters.summary: Wendell infiltrates a colonial records annex to find one unredacted shipping manifest proving Calloway Reach existed. Beat: triumph turning to ash when he discovers his own delivery logs were used to erase it.

chapters.title: Complicity
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV crisis: his thirty years of quiet routes made him an instrument of the cover-up. Sefa refuses to comfort him cheaply. Beat: guilt confronted honestly; she chooses to stay anyway.

chapters.title: Ashen Vale Boards
chapters.summary: Fleet inspectors seize the hauler mid-transit. Wendell talks his way through inspection while Sefa hides inside a cryo-seed pod. Beat: sustained terror; the first time they nearly lose each other.

chapters.title: The Neutral Assembly
chapters.summary: They learn of the Concord of Free Ports, a tribunal outside fleet law that convenes only during truce windows. Beat: hope with a deadline — forty days remain, and the Concord sits across hostile space.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: An old rival smuggler, Petra Quill, agrees to guide them through the blockade for a price: the vault's location. Wendell must weigh his sacred secret against Sefa's justice. Beat: sacrifice negotiated.

chapters.title: Through the Blockade
chapters.summary: Action chapter, alternating POVs: running dark between fleet pickets, a near-miss that kills their decoy drone, Sefa navigating by a dead language's star-charts. Beat: trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Vale's Doubt
chapters.summary: Commander Vale's POV: auditing the Calloway file, he finds his own father's signature on the erasure order. Beat: the antagonist fractures; duty begins to turn against itself.

chapters.title: The Price at Quill's Crossing
chapters.summary: Petra sells them out partially — taking payment from both sides. Fleet ambush at a refueling rock; Wendell wounded, the testimony archive damaged. Beat: betrayal, grief, and Sefa saving him.

chapters.title: Repairing the Dead
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Sefa restores corrupted testimony files while Wendell recovers, teaching her the extinct language's songs her grandmother sang. Beat: love declared plainly, without ceremony.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Final approach to the Concord as the truce window closes. Vale intercepts them — but instead of firing, demands to see the manifest. Beat: the hunter defecting, uncertain if it's mercy or another trap.

chapters.title: The Tribunal of Free Ports
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Sefa testifies in a language the Assembly must legally recognize under pre-Consolidation charter. Fleet lawyers move to dismiss; Vale corroborates the erasure order. Beat: justice argued word by word.

chapters.title: Entered Into Record
chapters.summary: Climax part two: the Assembly rules the massacre historically valid, but fleet hardliners move to destroy the archive physically. Wendell broadcasts the full testimony fleet-wide from the tribunal floor. Beat: truth made irreversible.

chapters.title: Living Proof
chapters.summary: Resolution: Wendell surrenders his ship and freedom to stand as custodian of the restored record, housed at the seed vault itself. Sefa chooses to remain with him. Beat: bittersweet peace; solitude exchanged for shared purpose.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV: seasons later, colonists arrive at the vault seeking their erased history, and Wendell opens the doors. A seed from Calloway Reach goes into soil. Beat: renewal — memory, like a seed, kept alive by hands willing to tend it.
